speculated.summary: Cleveland Independent School District near Houston restricted access to its networks and technology services after detecting suspicious activity. Schools stayed open, but visitor access was limited because the electronic visitor system was down.
speculated.speculation: A cyberattack on district systems.
speculated.official: The district describes it as an attempted cybersecurity intrusion and says a full breach of its systems has not been confirmed.
speculated.impact: Some district technology services offline; no restoration timeline given.
speculated.status: Under investigation. Breach not confirmed.

speculated.summary: The FAA halted departures across the U.S. for more than four hours after its air traffic communications network became unstable. It came one day after the big Microsoft outage, so many people asked whether the two were linked or whether someone had hacked the system.
speculated.speculation: A hack or coordinated attack on air traffic control, possibly connected to the Microsoft outage the day before.
speculated.official: The FAA says it has "no indication that this was a cyberattack or an outside nefarious actor." Its explanation: after a contractor installed a new router at a radio site in El Dorado, Arkansas, data flooded the FAA's legacy network (with a second problem site in Amarillo, Texas). Officials said it was not related to the Microsoft outage. On Nov. 18, the Director of National Intelligence and an FBI deputy director told Congress they had found no indication of malicious cyber activity behind the recent string of outages.
speculated.impact: Instability at 17 of 22 en route air traffic control centers; about 12,462 flights canceled that day (FAA figure).
speculated.status: No evidence of a hack. Root-cause investigation ongoing.

speculated.summary: Outlook email and other Microsoft 365 services went down worldwide for most of a business day, one of the largest outages in the company's history. Microsoft publicly pushed back on speculation that it had been hacked.
speculated.speculation: A cyberattack on Microsoft's cloud.
speculated.official: Microsoft's preliminary post-incident report calls it "a technical issue not related to cyber or AI/agents": a hidden bug from a July update, extra traffic after a Teams failover, and about 14% of gateway servers already offline combined to freeze its gateway servers.
speculated.impact: At the worst point more than 80% of the affected gateway servers stopped responding; it took nearly 24 hours to stabilize email.
speculated.status: Official cause published. Not a hack.

speculated.summary: A single update from security company CrowdStrike crashed Windows computers around the world, grounding flights and knocking banks, hospitals and broadcasters offline. It is still the go-to comparison whenever a big outage hits.
speculated.speculation: A global cyberattack.
speculated.official: CrowdStrike said the same day it was not a cyberattack. A faulty content update for its Falcon sensor caused Windows machines to crash.
speculated.impact: About 8.5 million Windows devices (Microsoft estimate).
speculated.status: Official cause published. Not a hack. (Older event, still widely referenced.)

speculated.summary: A failure in Amazon's biggest cloud region took down a long list of apps and websites for hours, leading many people to wonder if it was an attack on internet infrastructure.
speculated.speculation: A cyberattack or DNS hijacking.
speculated.official: AWS traced it to a hidden race condition in DynamoDB's automated DNS management that left a key DNS record empty. There was no sign of malicious activity.
speculated.impact: Widespread disruption to sites and apps that rely on AWS.
speculated.status: Official cause published. Not a hack.

speculated.summary: Nearly all of mainland Spain and Portugal lost power. In the first hours, a cyberattack was one of the theories openly discussed.
speculated.speculation: A cyberattack on the power grid.
speculated.official: Spain's government report (June 2025) and the European grid operators' expert panel final report (March 2026) found no evidence of a cyberattack. They blame voltage control problems and a chain of generator disconnections.
speculated.impact: Power cut across the Iberian Peninsula.
speculated.status: Official reports published. No cyberattack found. (Older event, final report in 2026.)

speculated.summary: Cloudflare, which sits in front of a huge share of websites, broke much of the web for several hours, including ChatGPT. Even Cloudflare's own team first suspected a massive DDoS attack.
speculated.speculation: A huge DDoS (traffic-flood) attack.
speculated.official: Cloudflare's postmortem says a database permission change made a configuration file for its bot-blocking system double in size, which crashed its core proxy software.
speculated.impact: Errors on a large share of websites using Cloudflare for several hours.
speculated.status: Official cause published. Not a hack.

speculated.org: Apple services outage (iCloud, App Store, Apple Pay)
speculated.summary: iCloud sign-in, the App Store, Apple Music, Apple Pay, AppleCare and Apple retail store systems went down for hours, the latest in a week of big U.S. outages.
speculated.speculation: Another hit in a coordinated cyberattack behind the Microsoft, FAA, Chase and NSA outages.
speculated.official: Apple said an internal update caused the outages and that it was not a cyberattack. The U.S. Director of National Intelligence also said the recent string of outages was not a cyberattack or a coordinated nation-state effort.
speculated.impact: Hours of sign-in failures and service outages; Apple stores unable to complete purchases. Services restored by that evening.
speculated.status: Company explanation given. Not a hack.

speculated.summary: Workday's HR platform went down for most of a day starting the afternoon of Nov. 13, leaving employees at customer organizations unable to clock in or out, see pay information, request time off or file for benefits. It hit one day after the Microsoft 365 outage and the same day as the FAA ground stop, during a run of big outages that drew hack theories online.
speculated.speculation: A cyberattack, possibly connected to the other outages that week.
speculated.official: Workday said the outage was not related to a cybersecurity incident. Its status notice said tenanted services at its disaster recovery site unexpectedly connected to production databases while it was validating a weekly maintenance window, leaving data inconsistent, so it put all WD1 production tenants into maintenance.
speculated.impact: Workday serves about 11,500 organizations; it has not said how many were affected. Service was restored by 11 a.m. ET on Nov. 14.
speculated.status: Company explanation given. Not a hack.

speculated.summary: Chase's online banking slowed and transactions were delayed for hours, with knock-on delays at other banks. It was the fourth big U.S. outage in five days, which fed questions about a coordinated attack. On Nov 17 a new ransomware gang, n0n, listed JPMorgan Chase on its leak site, claiming it stole data; on Nov. 19 the bank confirmed a separate attack on its vendors, which it says is unrelated to the outage.
speculated.speculation: A cyberattack on the banking system, possibly linked to the Microsoft and FAA outages.
speculated.official: Chase blamed a temporary software bug in on-premise hardware and said there was no evidence of a cyberattack. On Nov. 19 the bank confirmed a separate cyberattack on third-party vendors (see the confirmed list) and said there is "no connection" between it and the service disruption.
speculated.impact: Delayed transactions and online banking problems; some other banks affected when dealing with Chase.
speculated.status: Company explanation given. No evidence of a hack.

speculated.summary: Verizon customers across the U.S. lost wireless service for hours.
speculated.speculation: A cyberattack on the phone network.
speculated.official: Verizon blamed a "software issue"; reports cited law-enforcement sources saying there was no indication of a cyberattack. Verizon offered affected customers a $20 credit.
speculated.impact: Hours-long loss of service for customers nationwide.
speculated.status: Company explanation given. No evidence of a hack.

speculated.summary: The National Security Agency's internal top-secret network, NSANet, went down right on the heels of a week of big outages and stayed disrupted for nearly four days. It was restored on Nov. 20.
speculated.speculation: An attack on a U.S. intelligence network.
speculated.official: The NSA described it as scheduled maintenance. Multiple U.S. officials told CNN it was not a cyberattack and appears tied to the agency's patching of recently disclosed vulnerabilities in PHP software; a senior administration official said the restoration work was going "slower than expected." At a Nov. 18 House hearing, U.S. intelligence and FBI officials said they had seen no indication of malicious cyber activity in the recent outages.
speculated.impact: Large parts of the NSA workforce sent home for days. The outage also hit NSA Georgia, which supports Middle East operations; officials say the agency's most sensitive intelligence systems kept working and backups were used. On Nov. 20 NSA told staff it was operating under "normal conditions with exceptions," with staggered building openings to avoid a login surge.
speculated.status: Network restored Nov. 20. Officials attribute it to patching problems; no evidence of a hack.

speculated.summary: SpaceX's Starlink satellite internet went down worldwide for hours, prompting talk of an attack.
speculated.speculation: A cyberattack on the satellite network.
speculated.official: SpaceX said a failed software upgrade to its ground-based network systems caused the outage.
speculated.impact: Global loss of Starlink service for hours.
speculated.status: Company explanation given. Not a hack.

speculated.summary: The Gentlemen ransomware gang listed Nvidia as a victim on its leak site, claiming it would post data soon and giving the company about nine days to pay. It has not posted any samples.
speculated.speculation: That the gang breached Nvidia and stole its data.
speculated.official: Nvidia says it is "investigating an incident that may have affected a third-party partner" and has "found no indication that Nvidia systems or networks were affected."
speculated.impact: Unknown. The gang's data claim is unverified.
speculated.status: Under investigation. No evidence Nvidia's own systems were hacked.

speculated.summary: Three days after the FAA ground stop, a United system outage delayed departures because pilots couldn't get final aircraft weight data needed for takeoff.
speculated.speculation: Another attack on U.S. aviation, linked to the FAA ground stop.
speculated.official: United said it was a technology issue, resolved in about an hour and a half, with no indication of a cyberattack or link to the ground stop.
speculated.impact: Delays to hundreds of departures.
speculated.status: No root cause published. No evidence of a hack.

speculated.summary: Marriott.com and the Bonvoy app wouldn't let members sign in for several hours, knocking out mobile check-in and digital room keys for some guests.
speculated.speculation: Part of a wave of attacks behind the week's other outages.
speculated.official: Marriott said it resolved a technical issue and its review found no indication it was cybersecurity-related.
speculated.impact: Several hours of failed log-ins, mobile keys and reservation changes.
speculated.status: Company explanation given. No evidence of a hack.

speculated.summary: The FAA briefly stopped all American Airlines departures nationwide after an IT problem. It came during a week of several big outages.
speculated.speculation: A cyberattack, possibly part of a wider campaign that week.
speculated.official: American described a technology issue affecting connectivity for some systems. It has not named a cause, and there is no public evidence of an attack.
speculated.impact: Nationwide departure halt of roughly 45 minutes, with delays after.
speculated.status: No root cause published. No evidence of a hack.

speculated.org: Xbox sign-in and game library outage
speculated.summary: Xbox players couldn't sign in, buy or launch games for many hours; even some disc games failed license checks.
speculated.speculation: An attack on Microsoft's gaming network during a cluster of outages.
speculated.official: Microsoft's Xbox CTO said a licensing service that Xbox depends on began failing.
speculated.impact: Sign-in, purchase and game launch failures from late July 26 into July 27.
speculated.status: Company explanation given. Not attributed to a hack.

speculated.summary: PlayStation Network accounts, gaming, the store and other features were down for about five hours.
speculated.speculation: A hack of Sony's network.
speculated.official: Sony has not published a root cause. Some outlets speculated about a cloud provider problem, which Sony did not confirm.
speculated.impact: About five hours of disruption across PSN services.
speculated.status: Cause not disclosed. No public evidence of a hack.

speculated.summary: In late August, refrigeration at at least six on-base grocery stores (commissaries) across the U.S. failed at nearly the same time. At one, freezers were put into defrost mode overnight and food melted.
speculated.speculation: A cyberattack on the commissaries' refrigeration controls, similar to the attacks that later hit French and European supermarket freezers.
speculated.official: Reuters reported on Oct. 29 that the Pentagon is treating the malfunctions as a suspected hack, citing four officials. The Pentagon says a Cyber Command unit is working with law enforcement partners, and Army CID's Cyber Field Office is working with French law enforcement. As of Nov. 4, officials had not confirmed whether anything malicious happened.
speculated.impact: Meat, dairy, produce and frozen food spoiled or pulled from sale at at least six commissaries. The Pentagon has not said how many stores were affected or how much food was lost.
speculated.status: Under investigation. Cause not officially determined.

speculated.summary: The New Plymouth School District shut down its network, school computers and Google accounts after detecting what it called a cyber threat within its network, and canceled classes for two days.
speculated.speculation: A cyberattack on the district's network; the district warned families to delete suspicious emails that appeared to come from the district or its schools.
speculated.official: The district calls it a potential cyber threat and says there is no evidence any data was compromised. Systems were shut down out of caution while it restores the network and checks devices.
speculated.impact: Classes canceled Nov. 11 and 12; school was set to resume as scheduled Nov. 16.
speculated.status: District investigating. No breach confirmed.

speculated.summary: A cybercrime group called Inception listed payroll company Paychex on its leak site around Nov. 17 and later marked the data as leaked. On Nov. 19 a former employee filed a proposed class action in Monroe County, N.Y., based on the group's claims.
speculated.speculation: That Inception broke into Paychex's network and stole about 68 GB of company data.
speculated.official: Paychex had not publicly acknowledged a breach as of the lawsuit filing and did not immediately respond to reporters.
speculated.impact: Unverified. The lawsuit says the claimed data includes employee Social Security numbers and bank account details, HR and benefits rosters naming about 1,000 people, client agreements and IT system diagrams.
speculated.status: Not confirmed by Paychex. Lawsuit filed; the group's claims are unverified.

speculated.summary: The official website of Brazil's Alagoas state government went offline on the morning of Nov. 20. Before it went down, the home page displayed the name "PERIODICCC," reportedly the identification of whoever was responsible.
speculated.speculation: A defacement: that someone broke in and altered the site's home page.
speculated.official: The state communications department (Secom) confirmed the site was down after a possible hacker attack and called in the state IT institute (Itec) to fix it.
speculated.impact: State government site unavailable for an indefinite period.
speculated.status: Under investigation; not officially confirmed as a hack.

speculated.summary: The INC Ransom gang listed Boeing on its leak site, claiming it took more than 3.6 million files from seven production servers and "33 years of operational data," and posted 10 screenshots as proof. Cybernews researchers say the samples may be linked to subsidiary Boeing Sikorsky Aircraft Support, which maintains military helicopters.
speculated.speculation: That the gang breached Boeing or one of its units and stole internal data.
speculated.official: Boeing had not commented as of Cybernews' report.
speculated.impact: Unknown. Screenshots show employee emails, board-meeting participant details, financial file names and a vendor list; the claimed scope cannot be independently verified.
speculated.status: Unverified gang claim; not confirmed by Boeing.

confirmed.summary: Kern Medical, the public hospital run by the Kern County Hospital Authority, says it found unusual activity on Sept. 17 and that an unauthorized third party copied files with patient information. According to its breach notice as reported by HIPAA Journal, an attacker posing as IT staff phoned an employee and tricked them into changing their account login settings, then got into that employee's Microsoft 365 and storage account and copied data on Sept. 16–17. It announced the breach on Nov. 16.
confirmed.impact: Patients' names, addresses, birth dates, medical record numbers, dates of service and health insurance information, plus Social Security numbers in limited cases. Number of people not disclosed.
confirmed.status: Confirmed by Kern Medical, which reported it to the FBI's IC3, reset the account's credentials, tightened authentication and monitoring, and is notifying patients; one year of credit monitoring offered where SSNs were involved.

confirmed.org: POSTECH (Pohang University of Science and Technology, South Korea)
confirmed.summary: South Korean research university POSTECH says an outside attacker exploited security flaws in its research equipment portal and IT service portal between 12:30 and 3:30 a.m. on Nov. 13, got administrator rights and viewed personal data. The break-in came to light while staff looked into an illegal cryptocurrency mining program found on a lab GPU server.
confirmed.impact: 19,500 university account IDs with encrypted passwords and 478 records of IDs, email addresses and affiliations. On Nov. 20 it found a further 25,551 records (names, emails, departments, positions and office extensions) leaked from its university business portal. No resident registration or passport numbers.
confirmed.status: Confirmed by POSTECH, which forced a password reset for all accounts and reported to the Personal Information Protection Commission and Ministry of Education.

confirmed.org: accesso ticketing system (LEGOLAND Korea Resort and SEA LIFE Busan)
confirmed.summary: An outsider got into the ticketing system run by accesso, the reservation vendor for LEGOLAND Korea Resort and SEA LIFE Busan Aquarium, on Nov. 14 by exploiting a weakness, and looked up some annual pass holders' details. Both attractions posted notices on Nov. 16 warning customers their data may have leaked.
confirmed.impact: Some annual (season) pass holders' names, encrypted birth dates, addresses, email addresses, phone numbers and annual pass barcode numbers. Number of people affected still under investigation; no evidence card or bank data was exposed.
confirmed.status: Confirmed by LEGOLAND Korea and SEA LIFE Busan. accesso removed the vulnerable endpoint and blocked the source addresses; investigation ongoing.

confirmed.org: ZOZO (ZOZOTOWN and WEAR, Japan, via PLAID KARTE)
confirmed.summary: Japanese online fashion retailer ZOZO says data it kept in KARTE, the PLAID marketing service hacked on Nov. 13, leaked. PLAID's investigation showed on Nov. 15 that part of ZOZO's customer data had been taken from PLAID's databases; ZOZO announced it on Nov. 20.
confirmed.impact: About 15.18 million ZOZOTOWN customers (including former members): internal member IDs, age, gender and postal code; for about 47,000 of them also display names, email addresses and phone numbers. About 13.93 million WEAR by ZOZO members' internal IDs, age and gender. About 24,000 brand staff records (member IDs, company names and names). ZOZO says passwords were not stored in KARTE and no card data leak has been found.
confirmed.status: Confirmed by ZOZO. No secondary damage found so far; affected people being notified.

confirmed.org: Infcurion Wallet Station (payment app platform, Japan; Payどん, AEON Pay)
confirmed.summary: Japanese fintech Infcurion says a third party broke into Wallet Station, the platform companies use to run their own smartphone payment apps, and personal data of app users leaked. It detected a flood of access on the night of Nov. 19, blocked the attacker's traffic, applied an emergency vulnerability patch and cut off service to the affected clients.
confirmed.impact: Up to about 250,000 users' records. Payどん, the Kagoshima payment app run by four local banks, says 251,172 records leaked, including names, birth dates, email addresses, passwords, account information, point balances and transaction history; it stopped all services on the morning of Nov. 20. AEON Pay suspended some code payments and donations during emergency maintenance but says it has found no leak of its customers' data.
confirmed.status: Confirmed by Infcurion and the Payどん banks. No misuse of the data found so far; investigation ongoing and no restart date set.

confirmed.summary: Korean online grocer Kurly says an outside attacker got into its systems on Nov. 17 by an abnormal method, stole authentication credentials and used them to reach internal business systems. It blocked the intrusion and reported it to authorities on Nov. 18.
confirmed.impact: Personal data of 10,699 people in its curator (influencer) program: names, user IDs, phone numbers, email addresses and social media details, plus bank account numbers and resident or business registration numbers for some. Membership numbers of two regular customers also leaked.
confirmed.status: Confirmed by Kurly, whose CEO apologized. Offering affected curators 50,000 to 150,000 won and promising full compensation for any resulting losses.

confirmed.org: Meta M (call center outsourcer, South Korea; Coinone, Bunjang, Mega MGC Coffee)
confirmed.summary: Meta M, which runs customer service centers for about 150 companies, says an outside party broke into its systems early on Nov. 12, and phone numbers and counseling conversations were viewed or taken from some systems. Clients including crypto exchange Coinone, resale app Bunjang and Mega MGC Coffee have reported leaks.
confirmed.impact: Varies by client. Coinone says up to 11 kinds of information customers gave during support calls may have leaked, including names, phone numbers, resident registration numbers, account numbers, passwords and wallet addresses. Bunjang says 49 phone numbers leaked; Mega MGC Coffee says 30. As of Nov. 20 about 10 client companies had reported leaks to regulators (Herald Business).
confirmed.status: Confirmed by Meta M and affected clients. Reported to KISA; KISA and the Personal Information Protection Commission are investigating.

confirmed.summary: Jeonju University says its online liberal arts course service (AHA) was hacked at about 11:42 p.m. on Nov. 16. It confirmed the leak about 16 hours later, blocked outside access and reported it to regulators. It came a day after the Jeonbuk education office's school bus system breach.
confirmed.impact: About 180,000 records, including about 25,000 resident registration numbers, of current and former students, staff and old website members. Leaked items include passwords, addresses, phone numbers and disability status.
confirmed.status: Confirmed by Jeonju University. Reported to the Personal Information Protection Commission, KISA and the Ministry of Education.

confirmed.summary: Senior care company Caring says an outside attacker bypassed authentication and got into an internal data lookup tool between Aug. 11 and Sept. 3. It closed the hole on Sept. 4 and at first thought no personal data was viewed, but a later review found the attacker had looked up records using existing accounts. It confirmed the leak on Nov. 17 and reported it to KISA.
confirmed.impact: Elderly clients, guardians, care workers, some job seekers and staff. Names, birth dates, addresses and contact details, long-term care numbers and grades, and for some clients health details such as major illnesses, blood pressure and cognitive function. Some resident registration numbers, account numbers and passwords written in free-text notes also leaked. Total number not disclosed.
confirmed.status: Confirmed by Caring. Affected people being notified; investigation ongoing.

confirmed.summary: Norwegian says one of its external IT suppliers was hit by a cyberattack and malicious code was placed on parts of its website for a limited time on the afternoon and evening of Monday, Nov. 16. It found out on Nov. 18 and switched off the affected technology.
confirmed.impact: About 5,000 customers who used the website in that window; card numbers, expiry dates and CVC codes may be exposed. Norwegian emailed them asking them to block their cards.
confirmed.status: Confirmed by Norwegian. Says the breach has been stopped and the website is safe to use. Separate from the Amadeus booking data leak.

confirmed.org: Ransomware network extorting U.S. firms (Ukraine arrests)
confirmed.summary: Ukraine's Prosecutor General's Office, working with the FBI, said police arrested four suspected key members of a ransomware group of at least 27 people, part of a wider network of more than 60 that includes former Conti members. Police say the group posed as IT support to trick employees into handing over logins or installing remote access tools, then stole data and encrypted systems.
confirmed.impact: Authorities say at least 28 companies were extorted for a combined $40.5 million. Ukrainian court records name U.S. targets including Warren Oil, Maxxis International-USA, Newpark Resources and Quantum Health (The Record).
confirmed.status: Confirmed by Ukrainian law enforcement. Four suspects face up to 15 years in prison; 66 searches carried out and cash, devices and bank cards seized. Ransomware strain not named.

confirmed.summary: Lithuania's customs agency says attackers gained unauthorized access to BAP, the portal people and businesses use to log in to customs and some European Commission customs systems. It shut the portal down after detecting the attack on Nov. 10. Its chief called it a targeted, sophisticated attack that tried to go deeper into more sensitive systems.
confirmed.impact: Possible data breach affecting several hundred people and businesses who logged in on Nov. 9-10; local media say names, addresses, phone numbers, emails and personal ID numbers may be exposed. Access to EU customs systems including ICS2 was disrupted for some users.
confirmed.status: Confirmed by Lithuanian Customs. Services partly restored as of Nov. 16; attackers and vulnerability not identified.

confirmed.summary: Police say unknown attackers got into parts of the IT systems of Neuried, a town in Baden-Württemberg, and left a message there. The mayor discovered the attack on Nov. 17 and the affected systems were shut down as a precaution.
confirmed.impact: Town hall not reachable by email. Police say early findings show data was taken, but what and how much is unclear.
confirmed.status: Confirmed by police and the municipality. Investigation ongoing.

confirmed.org: Amadeus booking system (via Norwegian, Widerøe, SAS)
confirmed.summary: Spanish travel booking platform Amadeus reported a security incident in which an unauthorized actor had access to its systems for at least three years, Norway's National Security Authority (NSM) says. Amadeus says a vulnerability in its booking display system made certain booking data accessible; it was closed on Sept. 23, 2026. The breach became known in Norway on Oct. 27.
confirmed.impact: Depending on the booking: identity and itinerary, passport number and nationality, contact details, ticket and flight numbers, seats and free-text notes. Norwegian told Norway's data protection authority 144,249 Norwegian and Widerøe passengers are affected; NRK reports SAS has said 350,000 of its passengers in four countries are affected. NSM says travel of 75 Norwegian public and private organizations was exposed. No payment data reported taken.
confirmed.status: Confirmed by Amadeus, NSM and affected airlines. Amadeus says the attacker no longer has access.

confirmed.summary: New Zealand environmental advocacy group Forest & Bird says hackers got into its systems and accessed supporters' details. It was alerted on the evening of Nov. 18, and a forensic search of its website found malicious files hidden there to read data.
confirmed.impact: Mainly names, phone numbers and email addresses. The group says a "small subset" of people may also have had payment card details, birth dates and physical addresses taken. Number of people affected not yet known.
confirmed.status: Confirmed by Forest & Bird. Unauthorized access blocked and malicious files removed; NZ Police, the National Cyber Security Centre and the Privacy Commissioner notified. Investigation ongoing.

confirmed.summary: A cyber incident knocked out the district's communications systems and much of its technology, including phones and internet access, and forced all Perry Local buildings to close on Monday, Nov. 16. On Nov. 18 the district said its investigation found malware caused the incident.
confirmed.impact: All schools closed for a day. The district says there is no evidence personally identifiable information was released. Schools reopened Nov. 17 after critical systems were restored.
confirmed.status: Confirmed by the district (malware). Ohio Cyber Integration Center contacted and the Ohio Cyber Reserve engaged.

confirmed.org: Money Forward (fintech, Japan, via Notion and Fireworks AI)
confirmed.summary: Money Forward said some Notion AI chat records from three of its group companies may have leaked after hackers broke into Fireworks AI, the provider Notion used to process its AI features. Notion told the company on Nov. 10. Money Forward says its own services and systems were not accessed.
confirmed.impact: Personal information on 4,797 customers and business contacts (names, email addresses, internal system IDs) plus some employee names and emails, from chat records created Oct. 5 to 24. No passwords or card data involved; no misuse found.
confirmed.status: Confirmed by Money Forward. Reported to Japan's Personal Information Protection Commission; affected people being notified.

confirmed.summary: Quantum Systems, which builds reconnaissance drones used by Germany's military and Ukraine, said it found an active cyberattack by hostile actors at the end of October. According to Der Spiegel and the Financial Times, attackers planted a malicious file disguised as an update to its QBase mission-planning software on the company's update server; it reached some customer servers, including German military ones, but not the drones.
confirmed.impact: German armed forces grounded their Quantum Systems drones as a precaution and left them out of an exercise; the drones have since returned to flight. The company says there is no risk in operating its systems.
confirmed.status: Confirmed by Quantum Systems. Contained; German military counterintelligence, domestic intelligence and the federal cybersecurity agency are investigating. Attackers not publicly identified.

confirmed.summary: Hackers drained about $6.3 billion in crypto from Binance's hot wallets, the largest crypto theft on record. Blockchain analysts traced it to North Korea's TraderTraitor group.
confirmed.impact: About $6.3 billion stolen. Binance says it covered all losses and resumed withdrawals.
confirmed.status: Confirmed by Binance. Losses covered.

confirmed.summary: Attackers got in through the platform of one of the bank's service providers and used Crédit Mutuel Arkéa's own account to send money to other banks, which was then converted into cryptocurrency. The bank suspended some transactions as a precaution and its app was unavailable for several hours.
confirmed.impact: More than €100 million taken, an order of magnitude the bank confirms (Le Télégramme reports €118 million; the bank has not confirmed that figure). Part of the money has been blocked or recovered. The bank says no customer accounts were used and customers' funds are not affected; some transfers were delayed.
confirmed.status: Confirmed by Crédit Mutuel Arkéa. Paris prosecutor's office opened an investigation, led by France's anti-cybercrime office (OFAC). Recovery efforts ongoing.

confirmed.summary: The ShinyHunters gang stole data from Canvas, the school platform used by thousands of schools and universities, then defaced login pages during finals. Instructure later reached an agreement with the hackers.
confirmed.impact: Names, emails, student IDs and some private messages. Hackers claimed 275 million users; TechCrunch reported more than 30 million students and staff.
confirmed.status: Confirmed by Instructure.

confirmed.summary: The FBI declared a "major cyber incident" and notified Congress after a suspected China-linked breach of a system tied to wiretaps and surveillance targets.
confirmed.impact: Possible exposure of surveillance-target information; full scope not disclosed.
confirmed.status: Confirmed by the FBI. Investigation ongoing.

confirmed.summary: Iran-linked hackers (Handala) took over admin accounts and remotely wiped tens of thousands of company devices, disrupting operations for weeks.
confirmed.impact: Roughly 80,000 devices wiped (BleepingComputer); fully operational again about three weeks later.
confirmed.status: Confirmed by Stryker. Recovered.

confirmed.summary: Chinese state-linked hackers stole credentials from ConnectWise's cloud backup service and used them to get into customers' Microsoft 365 accounts, spying on thousands of companies.
confirmed.impact: Customer Microsoft 365 tenants (email and files) potentially accessed; Cloud Backup taken offline.
confirmed.status: Confirmed by ConnectWise and Microsoft.

confirmed.summary: Expedia Group, owner of Expedia, Hotels.com and Vrbo, confirmed attackers reached its systems through a compromised third-party data platform provider in a supply chain attack that hit several companies. The n0n extortion group claims it stole more than 1 TB of Expedia data. Security researchers had described a similar attack using access tied to the Qubole data platform; Expedia has not named the vendor.
confirmed.impact: Not disclosed by Expedia. n0n claims (unverified) hundreds of millions of account records and about 830 million rows of loyalty program data, plus traveler profiles and trip records.
confirmed.status: Breach confirmed by Expedia. Scale and n0n's data claims unconfirmed; investigation ongoing.

confirmed.summary: Attackers exploited a flaw in Optimizely's Web Experimentation platform to inject malicious JavaScript into scripts that run on customers' websites. Researchers at Report URI found the code on 178 organizations' sites, including big names like Salesforce, Zoom, HSBC, CNN and Ikea, so visitors to those sites were exposed without the companies themselves being breached.
confirmed.impact: Per Report URI, the malware swapped crypto wallet addresses, skimmed payment cards, stole cookies and screenshots, and tried to deliver iOS exploit kits to iPhones and iPads; at least $7,000 in crypto was traced as stolen. Most of the malicious code was removed the same day.
confirmed.status: Confirmed by Optimizely. In a Nov. 18 update it said under 5% of its customers were affected, the flaw (in its Web Experimentation sign-up flow) was closed within three hours of detection, and all injected code has been removed.

confirmed.org: PLAID KARTE customers (MUFG Bank, JINS, Shimamura and others, Japan)
confirmed.summary: Attackers exploited a vulnerability in servers run by PLAID, the Tokyo company behind the KARTE customer-data marketing service, stole credentials used to connect to its systems and databases, and read data out. They also took over a PLAID account to get into the admin console. PLAID shut down all KARTE services on Nov. 13, and companies that use KARTE have been announcing leaks of their own customers' data since. On Nov. 20 PLAID said about 2,200 client companies in total (counting overlaps) had data leaked or possibly leaked.
confirmed.impact: Varies by company. MUFG Bank: about 6.5 million records of gender, age and region (no names or contact details). JINS: up to about 18.29 million accounts (email, surname, birth date and more). Shimamura: about 7 million members' birth dates, gender, prefecture and postal code. RIZAP: up to about 4.32 million email addresses. J.League: about 2.38 million ticketing records (internal user IDs, birth dates, gender, prefecture and city). Stripe International: about 150,000 STRIPE CLUB records with email addresses and member IDs. Wacoal: internal IDs, ages, birth dates and gender possibly leaked (count still under investigation). NTT Solmare: up to about 1.17 million MangaPlaza records and up to about 130,000 Comic Cmoa records (hashed member numbers, birth dates, gender and more). Sharp: up to about 3.26 million online store customers' ages, birth dates and other details (NHK). Uniform Next: up to about 1.7 million customer records (company names, names, email addresses, phone numbers, postal codes, job types and industries; no passwords, card data or addresses). Sumitomo Mitsui Banking Corp. (SMBC): up to about 14 million records of birth dates, gender and whether a phone number is registered (not linked to names; Nikkei). Goldwin: about 3.67 million Goldwin Members email addresses, birth dates, gender, prefecture and activity data (no names, card data or passwords). Mainichi Shimbun: about 140,000 Mainichi Shimbun Digital members' surnames, plus ages, plan names, point-club IDs or email addresses for some. ZOZO: about 15.18 million ZOZOTOWN and 13.93 million WEAR member records (see separate entry). Tokyo Gas also confirmed customer data leaked, with numbers still under investigation. PLAID also says credentials used to link KARTE to outside services leaked, and has asked customers to revoke them.
confirmed.status: Confirmed by PLAID and affected companies. PLAID says about 2,200 client companies (2,220 counting overlaps) may be affected, including 570 whose linked customer data may have leaked; it plans to give clients detailed data from Nov. 24, expects to restart KARTE in mid-January, and now forecasts a full-year net loss of about ¥2 billion (Nikkei).

confirmed.summary: Attackers got into a test-environment system at Rakuten Securities on Nov. 11 and customer data held there may have been taken. The company detected the intrusion on Nov. 16 and blocked it.
confirmed.impact: Login IDs and customer codes for up to about 11.25 million accounts; names, birth dates, addresses, phone numbers, emails, employers, withdrawal bank accounts, and self-reported income and assets for up to about 4.47 million accounts. Rakuten says passwords and PINs were not leaked and no unauthorized trades have been found.
confirmed.status: Confirmed by Rakuten Securities. Investigation ongoing.

confirmed.summary: Unauthorized access to KARTE, a marketing service run by PLAID that DHC used for direct mail and similar messages, leaked DHC customer account information linked to it. PLAID notified DHC on Nov. 13.
confirmed.impact: About 19.11 million customer account records (names, email addresses, birth dates and more). DHC says online-shop passwords and card data were not included and no secondary damage has been confirmed.
confirmed.status: Confirmed by DHC. Regulator to be notified.

confirmed.summary: Hackers were inside DentaQuest's network for several days and stole personal and health data. It is the largest healthcare breach reported to U.S. regulators this year.
confirmed.impact: 15 million people (HHS filing).
confirmed.status: Confirmed. Notices sent.

confirmed.summary: Attackers broke into a Japanese newsletter service used by hundreds of brands, including SEGA, and took subscriber email lists.
confirmed.impact: 81,329,467 email addresses from up to about 380 client companies (company count; addresses, not people).
confirmed.status: Confirmed by ARARA. Investigation ongoing.

confirmed.summary: An intruder got into DriveWealth's network, which powers investing features in many apps, and accessed customer data including Social Security numbers.
confirmed.impact: 30 million people (state attorney general filings).
confirmed.status: Confirmed. Notices sent.

confirmed.summary: A company that scans driver's licenses for bars, stores and other businesses confirmed hackers copied ID data from its cloud. Hackers advertised photos of more than 150 million North American drivers.
confirmed.impact: 13 million people per a state filing; hackers claimed about 153 million records.
confirmed.status: Confirmed by IDScan.net.

confirmed.summary: Hackers poisoned an update of Trivy, a popular security tool, to steal a European Commission cloud key, then took data from its cloud accounts.
confirmed.impact: About 340 GB of data, including personal data and email content; data of 30 EU entities exposed (CERT-EU).
confirmed.status: Confirmed by CERT-EU and the Commission.

confirmed.summary: The European Commission confirmed a cyberattack on Sysper, the internal HR platform staff use for salary information, leave requests, timesheets and training sign-ups. Spokesperson Thomas Regnier called it an "AI-generated cyber campaign" first detected on Oct. 22. POLITICO reported that CERT-EU linked the attackers to ARTEX, an open-source AI hacking platform; the Commission has not named the tool.
confirmed.impact: The Commission says it temporarily took several applications offline as a protective measure and most have since been restored. Personnel systems, including payroll, leave requests and medical reimbursements, were reportedly disrupted for more than 10 days. The Commission says it has notified affected individuals and found no evidence of a data breach affecting staff as a whole. No ransom demand is known.
confirmed.status: Confirmed by the European Commission on Nov. 19. Investigation ongoing; not attributed to any actor.

confirmed.summary: A coordinated, destructive attack hit more than 30 wind and solar farms and a major combined heat and power plant. Poland's CERT linked it to Russian state hackers.
confirmed.impact: Communications disrupted at some grid connection points; power and heat generation did not stop.
confirmed.status: Confirmed by CERT Polska and the Polish government.

confirmed.summary: U.S. agencies warned that Iran-affiliated hackers were breaking into internet-exposed control equipment (PLCs) at water and wastewater systems and other critical infrastructure, causing operational disruption.
confirmed.impact: Operational disruption at affected utilities; no single total published.
confirmed.status: Confirmed by CISA, FBI, EPA and NSA advisories.

confirmed.summary: Norway's state-controlled oil and gas giant said it detected an ongoing cyberattack against some of its IT systems and was working to neutralise it.
confirmed.impact: Some IT systems affected; staff may have trouble reaching corporate apps and IT services. Equinor says there are still no signs data was leaked, the attack did not involve a computer virus, and oil and gas production is running as normal.
confirmed.status: Confirmed by Equinor. On Nov. 20 it said the attack had been stopped, production is running as normal, and there is no indication data was stolen or altered or that employees, partners or suppliers were affected. Reported to police; attackers not named.

confirmed.summary: Ransomware encrypted data on servers at Osaki Electric, a major Japanese maker of smart electricity meters. In a second report on Nov. 20 the company said the attacker most likely got in at about 1:30 a.m. on Nov. 15 by getting past the login on its VPN device, probably by trying passwords on an account that did not have multi-factor authentication, and then encrypted some virtual servers. It cut its systems off from outside networks on Nov. 17 and shut down production systems at its Saitama plant and two production subsidiaries.
confirmed.impact: Production and shipment of smart meters and other products suspended at the Saitama R&D and Manufacturing Center, Iwate Osaki Electric and Osaki Platech, with no restart date. On Nov. 19 Osaki found technical information that appears to come from its systems posted on a site believed to belong to the attacker; what else may have leaked is still under investigation. Osaki says its smart meters themselves were not affected and its backups are intact. Financial impact unknown.
confirmed.status: Confirmed by Osaki Electric, which reported it to police. Sankei reports the company was contacted by a party believed to be the attacker and says it will not negotiate. Recovery from backups under way; work to restart in stages once systems are confirmed safe.

confirmed.summary: A new ransomware gang called n0n listed Visa on its leak site and set a 48-hour deadline to publish data it claims to have stolen. Visa confirmed an incident, but says it started at an unnamed third-party service provider in the Asia Pacific region. On Nov. 19 the gang published a dataset tied to Visa's premium dining and loyalty programs in Asia-Pacific.
confirmed.impact: Visa says its own systems were not involved or impacted and there is no indication payment data such as card numbers was affected. The gang claims over 1.5 million cardholder interactions; Cybernews researchers who examined the leaked data found more than 6,000 premium Visa customers in it, with names, email addresses, phone numbers and booking details.
confirmed.status: Third-party incident confirmed by Visa. Gang has published data; its larger claims are unverified.

confirmed.summary: JPMorgan Chase said third parties that provide services to the bank were targeted in a cyberattack and that the attackers accessed certain marketing data held by those vendors. The ransomware gang n0n, which had listed the bank on its leak site, dumped data on Nov. 19 that Cybernews says is tied to the bank's invitation-only Reserve card program. BleepingComputer reports that n0n claimed an attack on cloud data analytics company Qubole on Nov. 11 and that Qubole is suspected to be the provider involved; JPMorgan, Visa and Mastercard have not named it.
confirmed.impact: JPMorgan says the marketing data may include some customer names and email addresses. Cybernews researchers found about 16,000 customer email addresses, some phone numbers and account IDs, and more than 100 bank employee email addresses in the leak. The bank says the attack has no connection to the service disruption some customers had earlier in the week.
confirmed.status: Vendor attack confirmed by JPMorgan Chase. Investigation ongoing; the gang's wider claims are unverified.

confirmed.summary: Mastercard said it was recently informed of an incident at a third-party provider that exposed a limited amount of information from a subset of cardholders enrolled in a specific benefit program. The ransomware gang n0n, which also listed Visa and JPMorgan Chase, had listed Mastercard on its leak site and published a dataset after its ransom deadline passed.
confirmed.impact: Mastercard says the exposed data was a limited amount of email addresses, not payment information, and there is no impact to its payment network or the ability to use cards. Cybernews says the leaked dataset has about 2,000 entries, poorly formatted and possibly test data; Reuters says it includes marketing data on customers in North America, the Middle East and Africa. Neither has verified it.
confirmed.status: Third-party incident confirmed by Mastercard, which says the exposure has been contained. The provider has not been named.

confirmed.org: SBC Medical Group (Shonan Beauty Clinic operator, Japan)
confirmed.summary: SBC Medical Group, which runs Shonan Beauty Clinic and other cosmetic and medical clinics in Japan, said attackers got into one of its customer databases after hammering the system from overseas with about 770,000 attempts overnight. It found the intrusion on Nov. 16 and cut the server off the network. Separately, attackers logged into the clinics' accounts on the outside booking service Tribeau (トリビュー) and took reservation data.
confirmed.impact: In a Nov. 18 SEC filing, SBC said basic personal information on about 1,624,000 people was taken from its database (names, contact details, birth dates, patient card numbers, member IDs, passwords and survey responses, not all items for everyone), plus 255,416 booking requests, 217,769 website inquiries and smaller sets of treatment-monitor and review records. It says about 20,000 employee account records (names, IDs, passwords) were also stolen, including bank account and tax information for 459 employees. From Tribeau: data on 12,641 people who booked and 6,804 who were treated (names in kana, phone numbers, ages, requested procedures, and for treated customers procedure names, dates and prices). SBC says electronic medical records were not taken.
confirmed.status: Confirmed by SBC Medical Group and Tribeau. Reported to Japan's privacy regulator and police; investigation ongoing.

sources.name: SBC Medical Group SEC filing release

confirmed.summary: An attacker exploited a flaw in the online banking platform Wellington IT provides to Irish credit unions and pulled saved payee records in early October. Credit unions were only told in mid-November.
confirmed.impact: About 40 credit unions affected, roughly a quarter of the country's total. Saved payee names, IBANs, BICs, addresses and payment references potentially exposed. Officials say member balances were not accessed and no financial losses have been reported.
confirmed.status: Confirmed by Wellington IT, affected credit unions and Ireland's government. Flaw closed. Wellington IT says it is working with the Data Protection Commission, NCSC and Garda cyber crime bureau; investigation ongoing.

confirmed.org: N-able Mail Assure and SpamExperts (email security cloud)
confirmed.summary: N-able said unknown attackers gained unauthorized access to a server in its Mail Assure and SpamExperts hosted cloud. A service disruption that started Nov. 16 was first traced to configuration and service dependencies, but the company later determined it was caused by the security incident and disabled management interfaces and APIs.
confirmed.impact: Management portal, APIs, quarantine and logging offline for Mail Assure and SpamExperts in the Americas, APAC and Europe; mail flow and filtering kept running. N-able says the incident was isolated to a single web server where the attacker may have been able to access certain credentials stored on the platform, and that it has no evidence so far that customer data or tenant mailboxes were accessed.
confirmed.status: Confirmed by N-able, which took the server offline, rotated internal credentials, revoked customer API tokens, invalidated OAuth tokens and reset local users' passwords. As of Nov. 20 remediation was progressing but portal and API access was still disabled; investigation ongoing.

confirmed.summary: Barracuda said an attacker used a cloud access key it had given a third-party vendor for a past project, and never retired, to get into about 10 of its cloud accounts over 44 hours on Nov. 1-2. The attacker moved through its data analytics environment, source-code repositories and Kubernetes clusters and went after cryptocurrency secrets. Barracuda says the intrusion matched the ARTEX AI penetration-testing framework.
confirmed.impact: About 10 cloud accounts accessed. The attacker reached a system storing customer integration credentials for Barracuda XDR; Barracuda found no evidence they were taken but asked potentially affected Managed XDR customers to revoke and recreate them.
confirmed.status: Confirmed by Barracuda. Attacker not named.

confirmed.summary: GitBook says an attacker used a flaw in its SSO login flow to create sessions as GitBook staff, then reached its internal code repositories, a Cloudflare API key and production secrets that gave full infrastructure access. GitBook says the attack appears aimed at one of its customers.
confirmed.impact: GitBook took its app offline for about 16 hours (Nov. 2-3) and rotated every infrastructure and customer-managed secret. It is treating all customer data as exposed, including API tokens, integration secrets, Git Sync secrets and authenticated docs. GitBook says billing information and passwords were not compromised and it found no evidence other customers' content was modified.
confirmed.status: Confirmed by GitBook in a published post-mortem. Resolved; the attacker has not been named.

confirmed.summary: South Korea's Ministry of the Interior and Safety said hackers got into the government's administrative email system by going through vulnerable local government networks and exploiting a flaw in its single sign-on (SSO) login system.
confirmed.impact: Abnormal access to about 300 government email accounts found so far. The breach was reported to the privacy regulator and affected people were notified.
confirmed.status: Confirmed by South Korea's government. Joint investigation with NIS and KISA ongoing.

confirmed.summary: Japan's biggest furniture chain found intruders in a company system and says customer and order records may have been stolen.
confirmed.impact: Up to 37.62 million potentially affected records (names, contact details, dates of birth); Nitori says the count includes duplicates and is not the number of people. No passwords or card numbers.
confirmed.status: Confirmed by Nitori, which says attackers extracted data through a vulnerability in an online-shop admin server. How much leaked is still undetermined.

confirmed.summary: The shipping giant confirmed that a threat actor breached a legacy system belonging to a company it previously acquired and stole data. The WhiteArmor ransomware group claimed the attack and threatened to release about 100GB of data, demanding $5 million (attacker's claim).
confirmed.impact: Maersk says the incident is isolated to a local system, current evidence indicates no sensitive data was disclosed, and shipping operations are not disrupted.
confirmed.status: Confirmed by Maersk. Investigation ongoing.

confirmed.summary: A cyberattack hit the Santos Port Authority (APS), the state-owned company that runs Brazil's largest port, knocking its online systems partly offline after a power outage at its headquarters. APS later confirmed a ransom demand. Brazil's Federal Police are investigating.
confirmed.impact: Port authority systems partly down for days; operators reported delays and manual scheduling, arrival records and billing. Terminals and ship movements kept running. APS says it does not know whether data was accessed.
confirmed.status: Confirmed by the port authority. Recovery ongoing; attacker not officially named.

confirmed.summary: Attackers exploited unknown flaws in Cisco's SD-WAN network gear to get admin control. CISA ordered federal agencies to patch within two days and hunt for intruders.
confirmed.impact: Unknown number of networks; Cisco Talos said the campaign went back to at least 2023.
confirmed.status: Confirmed by Cisco and CISA (Emergency Directive 26-03).

confirmed.summary: A cyberattack knocked out Boston Scientific's global network, halting manufacturing, orders and shipping for about two weeks.
confirmed.impact: Global operations disrupted until about September 9; expected material hit to 2026 results.
confirmed.status: Confirmed by Boston Scientific. Recovered.

confirmed.summary: Attackers tricked their way into an employee account and copied customer data. ShinyHunters claimed the attack; Carnival hasn't named a group.
confirmed.impact: 5,995,277 people; data may include government ID numbers.
confirmed.status: Confirmed by Carnival.

confirmed.org: Value Design Value Card (prepaid e-money service, Japan)
confirmed.summary: Attackers exploited a web-server vulnerability at Value Design, a PayCloud Holdings subsidiary that runs the Value Card house e-money service for retailers, and took card ID numbers, PINs and balance data. On Nov. 18 the company said a second server, for a site it runs for business customers, was also hit on Oct. 19 and payment codes were taken from it.
confirmed.impact: 1,424,748 Value Card records (card ID numbers, PINs and balances; 569,224 were issued cards) plus up to about 31,000 payment codes from the second server. The company says no names or other personal details were included; the leaked codes were invalidated Nov. 16.
confirmed.status: Confirmed by Value Design and PayCloud Holdings. Investigation ongoing.

confirmed.org: NTT Solmare Comic Cmoa (e-book store, Japan)
confirmed.summary: NTT Solmare shut down its Comic Cmoa e-book store on Oct. 15 after detecting possible unauthorized access to its servers, and later confirmed attackers got into its member information system and took data. The store has been brought back in stages, with a full reopening targeted for November.
confirmed.impact: Registration data for 319 members (email, hashed password, nickname, birth date, gender) and up to about 4.2 million records from system log files (email, nickname, birth date, gender; no passwords). No card data or purchase history leaked, the company says.
confirmed.status: Confirmed by NTT Solmare. Service partly restored.

confirmed.summary: NTT Docomo detected unauthorized outside access to its Docomo Online Shop and My docomo account site on Nov. 4 and shut down procedures on both early Nov. 5. The company later confirmed that some customer information was taken through the access.
confirmed.impact: Up to about 300,000 customers, including former subscribers: names, birth dates, addresses, phone numbers, email addresses, ID document numbers and plan details, plus bank account details for some. Docomo says no card data was leaked and plans to compensate affected people.
confirmed.status: Confirmed by NTT Docomo. Most My docomo procedures back since Nov. 9; online shop still in emergency maintenance as of Nov. 18. Investigation ongoing.

confirmed.summary: 2RedBeans (Embrace Inc.) said an unauthorized party got into one of its internal systems on Nov. 4 and copied member information before the access was detected and shut off on Nov. 5.
confirmed.impact: About 1.3 million member accounts: names, gender, age and birth date, location, profile answers, profile photos (including unapproved ones), email addresses, verified phone numbers, IP addresses, and reports and feedback with any attached screenshots. The company says passwords, payment details, government ID numbers and private messages were not involved.
confirmed.status: Confirmed by 2RedBeans. Reported to the FBI's IC3; review ongoing.

confirmed.summary: A cyberattack forced JLR to shut down car production for about six weeks. It later reported a heavy loss tied to the attack.
confirmed.impact: £196 million in costs reported for the quarter; production halted for weeks.
confirmed.status: Confirmed by JLR. Recovered. (Older event, still in the news.)

confirmed.summary: A ransomware attack on production systems forced Coca-Cola to pause fairlife milk production at all four U.S. plants.
confirmed.impact: U.S. production suspended; most production resumed by July 27.
confirmed.status: Confirmed by Coca-Cola (SEC filing).

confirmed.summary: Vanderbilt University in Nashville said on Nov. 9 it was responding to an active cyberattack affecting university devices, systems and cloud-based services, and told everyone to shut down university devices and get off campus Wi-Fi. The BYOD ransomware gang has claimed the attack; that claim has not been confirmed by the university.
confirmed.impact: Most systems were restricted for days. As of Nov. 18 almost all systems are back, but Microsoft OneDrive, SharePoint and Teams remain disabled, Box is due back by Nov. 20, and the university is contacting people with compromised laptops in batches. BYOD claims it stole Social Security numbers, names, email addresses and other data; Vanderbilt says it does not yet know what data, if any, was accessed.
confirmed.status: Confirmed by Vanderbilt. Working with federal law enforcement; investigation ongoing.

confirmed.summary: Ransomware hit a SoftBank-group cloud provider, encrypting customer virtual servers used by companies and local governments.
confirmed.impact: 495 companies and local governments disrupted.
confirmed.status: Confirmed by IDC Frontier. No ransom paid.

confirmed.summary: An outsider broke into the internal network that runs Japan's Fugaku supercomputer through a public status dashboard, tampered with internal servers, and took or may have taken user data. RIKEN shut Fugaku down to contain it.
confirmed.impact: 4,222 Fugaku users' names, email addresses and user IDs, plus details they entered when registering (addresses, affiliations, phone numbers and other attributes) and records of which type of ID document they used for verification. RIKEN also found that 430 private keys users had stored for connecting to other systems (such as other supercomputers and clouds) were gathered and moved, 233 of them without a passphrase. Fugaku operations suspended and all jobs halted.
confirmed.status: Confirmed by RIKEN. On Nov. 20 it said it had found traces of the intruder accessing the user data and is treating it as leaked; no misuse found beyond some connections made with stolen keys. Users are being contacted individually and asked to revoke and reissue keys. Police in Saitama and Hyogo briefed; Fugaku will restart only after public services are separated from the management network and servers rebuilt.

confirmed.summary: An attacker drained funds from market-maker accounts on Lighter, a decentralized perpetual futures exchange, after the accounts' API keys were exposed. Lighter says the affected accounts used signing code outside its official software kits that reused cryptographic nonces, letting the attacker rebuild private keys from public signatures and move funds out through a public pool.
confirmed.impact: Blockchain investigators traced about $10.4 million in USDC withdrawn; other researchers' estimate of $15.5 million is unconfirmed by Lighter. Lighter's security council returned about $5 million to the affected trader. Withdrawals were paused, then resumed the same day.
confirmed.status: Confirmed by Lighter, which says its protocol, smart contracts, infrastructure and official SDKs were not compromised.

confirmed.org: WS Audiology (hearing aid maker, parent of Widex and Signia)
confirmed.summary: WS Audiology said attackers gained unauthorized access to its customer relationship management environment and certain operational IT systems. It took some internal and customer-facing systems offline to contain the incident, disrupting the Widex MOMENT app, Widex Compass Cloud and Signia TeleCare for days.
confirmed.impact: Hearing aids themselves were not affected, but some users lost app-based controls and clinics lost remote-care tools while systems were restored in phases. On Nov. 18 the CEO said the financial impact would be limited, citing a fast response and cyber insurance.
confirmed.status: Confirmed by WS Audiology. Systems restored; investigation ongoing.

confirmed.org: Mitsui Shopping Park app (Mitsui Fudosan, Japan)
confirmed.summary: Mitsui Fudosan and Mitsui Fudosan Retail Management said a third party gained unauthorized access to the Mitsui Shopping Park app and leaked part of its point-program member data. They found the access on Nov. 18 and suspended the app the same day.
confirmed.impact: Member numbers, names, birth dates, addresses and email addresses. The companies say card data and passwords were not included; the number of affected members is still under investigation.
confirmed.status: Confirmed by Mitsui Fudosan. App suspended; regulator notified; intrusion route under investigation.

confirmed.summary: Transport for London said it spotted suspicious activity on its Oyster photocard website on Nov. 16, after photocard holders got unexpected emails asking them to create an account they already had. It took the photocard system offline and says unauthorized access to customers' web account details resulted.
confirmed.impact: About 265,000 photocard customers' names, email and home addresses, phone numbers, dates of birth and security questions and answers were compromised. TfL says no passwords, bank or payment card details, journey information, or names and birth dates of children with Zip Oyster cards were taken. The photocard website stays offline, so cards can't be applied for or renewed online.
confirmed.status: Confirmed by TfL. Reported to the ICO. Investigation ongoing.

confirmed.summary: KPMG Canada confirmed a data breach in which client tax documents were compromised, and is contacting affected clients. It is the latest in a string of breaches at Canadian professional services firms, including several big Bay Street law firms.
confirmed.impact: Client tax documents. KPMG has not said how many clients or files were affected or how the attackers got in. It says its monitoring shows the data is not available online or being misused.
confirmed.status: Confirmed by KPMG Canada. Clients being contacted.

confirmed.org: FFG Industries (Fukuoka Financial Group company, Japan)
confirmed.summary: Fukuoka Bank said a third party gained unauthorized access to a data analysis tool used by FFG Industries, a Fukuoka Financial Group company, to compile data from its ordering systems. The tool was set up and run by an outside contractor, and some information in the database it connected to may have leaked.
confirmed.impact: 1,221 business clients potentially affected: company names and addresses, contact names, email addresses and phone numbers, login IDs and hashed passwords, and meeting records. The bank says its core banking system and account information were not affected and no misuse has been found.
confirmed.status: Confirmed by Fukuoka Bank on Nov. 19. Cause, entry route and full scope still under investigation.

confirmed.summary: Ransom messages appeared on district laptops saying attackers had extracted sensitive data and encrypted critical files, and demanding contact within 72 hours to negotiate. The district took its internet offline, knocking out phones and email.
confirmed.impact: The attackers claim to have taken personal information of current and former students, staff and contractors; the district says affected systems held data such as Social Security numbers, driver's license numbers, health insurance numbers and limited medical information. Nearly a month later, network access, camera feeds and other systems were still not fully restored.
confirmed.status: Confirmed by the district, which is working with the FBI, Virginia State Police and CISA and offering free credit monitoring. Network rebuild ongoing.

confirmed.summary: Unidentified attackers have been hitting the IT infrastructure of the Swiss canton of Basel-Country since Sunday, Nov. 15, the Cantonal Chancellery said. Some servers were cut off from the internet as a countermeasure. On Nov. 20 the canton said forensic analysis showed the attackers got into a database of work permits for cross-border commuters and stole data.
confirmed.impact: Around 20 cantonal applications on six servers affected, including the tax calculator; servers are being reinstalled. Emergency and rescue services' IT was not affected. The canton says 97,000 records were stolen covering cross-border commuter permits (G permits) applied for since Nov. 28, 2016: names, home addresses, birth dates, marital status, job titles and federal migration system (ZEMIS) ID numbers, plus contact details of employers in the canton. The permit application platform is offline.
confirmed.status: Confirmed by the Cantonal Chancellery. Criminal complaint filed against unknown persons; Switzerland's cybersecurity office, the data protection supervisor, the foreign ministry and the German and French embassies informed. Analysis ongoing.

confirmed.summary: Stadtwerke Wittenberg confirmed that criminals attacked the systems of its regional internet and phone provider Wittenberg-Net overnight into Wednesday, Nov. 18, causing a widespread outage around Wittenberg in Saxony-Anhalt. All relevant systems were taken offline as a precaution.
confirmed.impact: About 8,000 households and many public facilities, including the Wittenberg city and district administrations, temporarily lost landline phone and internet service or had limited service. Most connections are back online; work on some systems continues.
confirmed.status: Confirmed by Stadtwerke Wittenberg. Recovery ongoing.

confirmed.summary: The ATF declared a "major incident" after a breach of a standalone system holding information on targets of its investigations. A ransomware gang (Qilin) claimed it; ATF has not confirmed who did it.
confirmed.impact: One standalone system; data taken not disclosed.
confirmed.status: Confirmed by ATF. Investigation ongoing.

confirmed.org: Japan health ministry drug supply system
confirmed.summary: Japan's Ministry of Health, Labour and Welfare said NTT Data, which runs and maintains its system for tracking drug supply shortages, reported unauthorized access by a third party. Traces show some stored data was viewed and someone tried to alter it, and a suspicious file was uploaded to the reporting system.
confirmed.impact: Names and contact details of some drug company staff may have leaked; full scope still under investigation. The system was shut down on Nov. 17 and the reporting system stays offline for now.
confirmed.status: Confirmed by the health ministry. Attacker IPs blocked and the file deleted; investigation ongoing.

sources.name: Ministry of Health, Labour and Welfare (Japanese)

confirmed.summary: Hackers got into three cloud servers belonging to an unnamed Gurugram-based digital payments firm on the night of Nov. 5-6, ran malicious scripts and abused its payout API to send money out of its escrow account, police say. Two men from Ludhiana have been arrested.
confirmed.impact: About ₹25.67 crore (police figure) taken in 265 unauthorized payments to 156 bank accounts; about ₹1.5 crore frozen so far.
confirmed.status: Confirmed by Gurugram police. Two arrests; money trail and how the servers were breached still under investigation.

confirmed.summary: Crypto hardware wallet maker Trezor says its shipping partner Skladon had unauthorized access to its systems on Nov. 7, and the attacker exported Trezor customer shipping data. Skladon notified Trezor on Nov. 15.
confirmed.impact: About 27,000 orders placed between Aug. 9 and Nov. 7, 2026: full names, phone numbers, delivery addresses, email addresses and order details. Trezor says its own systems were not compromised and no wallet backups, PINs or passphrases were involved, and it warns customers to watch for scams.
confirmed.status: Confirmed by Trezor. Investigation ongoing.

confirmed.summary: J.B. Hunt confirmed it is investigating unauthorized access to certain information in an isolated part of its technology systems. The WhiteArmor extortion group claims it stole data from J.B. Hunt as well as Ryder and Echo Global Logistics; those two have not publicly confirmed an incident.
confirmed.impact: Systems stayed operational. What was taken has not been disclosed; employees have filed multiple proposed class action lawsuits. The date shown is when ransomware trackers recorded the attack.
confirmed.status: Confirmed by J.B. Hunt. Investigation ongoing.

confirmed.summary: Singapore mobile carrier M1 disclosed a data breach it identified on October 30 involving customer information. It says the breach has been contained.
confirmed.impact: Customer names, NRIC/FIN numbers, dates of birth, mobile numbers, email addresses and addresses. M1 says no payment card, banking or account access was compromised; it has not said how many customers are affected.
confirmed.status: Confirmed by M1. Customers being notified.

confirmed.summary: Hackers used an old Klue credential to steal access keys, then pulled sales/CRM data from many Klue customers, including security companies like HackerOne and LastPass.
confirmed.impact: Close to 200 customer companies affected (TechCrunch); business contact and sales data.
confirmed.status: Confirmed by Klue and affected companies.

confirmed.summary: Apify, a Czech web scraping and browser automation platform, said an unauthorized third party got into parts of its internal systems on Nov. 9-10. It cut off the access, rotated internal secrets and API tokens, reset all sessions and revoked some third-party OAuth connections, including GitHub.
confirmed.impact: Affected customers' API tokens and proxy passwords rotated; some told to reset two-factor authentication because codes may have been exposed. Apify says passwords are safe and it has found no sign that account data on the platform was affected.
confirmed.status: Confirmed by Apify. Investigation ongoing.

confirmed.summary: Myriad Genetics detected unauthorized access to its IT network and temporarily suspended testing operations and order management systems while it contained the activity.
confirmed.impact: Testing temporarily paused. The company is still assessing whether patient records were accessed. Most systems back to normal.
confirmed.status: Confirmed by Myriad Genetics (SEC filing). Investigation ongoing.

confirmed.summary: Thai oil refiner Star Petroleum Refining told the Stock Exchange of Thailand it was hit by a cyberattack that gave attackers unauthorized access to company data.
confirmed.impact: Company data accessed; what and how much is still being investigated. SPRC says customer service and operations are not affected, and it can't yet assess any financial impact.
confirmed.status: Confirmed by SPRC. Investigation ongoing.

confirmed.org: OPEN Inc. BizRobo! mini (automation software, Japan)
confirmed.summary: An outside party got into the cloud environment that OPEN Inc. uses to run some of its services on Nov. 12, including the authentication server for its BizRobo! mini automation product. The company spotted a security alert on Nov. 16.
confirmed.impact: Logs show access to authentication IDs and passwords for about 560 customer companies (about 1,000 accounts). Other servers in the same environment were also accessed; impact on stored data is under investigation.
confirmed.status: Confirmed by OPEN Inc. Affected server isolated; emergency maintenance set for Nov. 21.

confirmed.summary: An outside party broke into systems at Openlogi, a Japanese warehouse and shipping service used by online stores, on Nov. 8-9 and took shipping data. Store clients including Kashima Antlers FC, United Arrows' overseas shops, REALITY Studios, Toei Animation's online lottery shop and Calpis's butter online shop have since warned their customers.
confirmed.impact: Recipient names, addresses, phone numbers, email addresses and product details from shipments requested Apr. 8 to Nov. 8, 2026. Total count still under investigation; Kashima Antlers alone reports 40,844 affected people and Toei Animation 3,358. No credit card numbers.
confirmed.status: Confirmed by Openlogi and client companies. Access route blocked Nov. 9.

confirmed.summary: Atlas, which runs the Confit system that Japanese academic societies use for conferences, says an attacker abroad exploited a flaw in how one optional feature checked users and their permissions, likely found by scanning broadly for weaknesses with AI or similar tools, and pulled presenter information it should not have been able to see.
confirmed.impact: About 10,000 records covering 62 academic societies: presentation titles, presenter names, affiliations and presenter email addresses. No payment card, driver's license or My Number data.
confirmed.status: Confirmed by Atlas. Temporary block in place since Nov. 12, permanent fix expected Nov. 20; reported to police and Japan's privacy regulator.

confirmed.summary: Hackers breached Fireworks AI, a tech provider, and used stolen credentials to reach Uber data. Notion was also affected.
confirmed.impact: 149,346 Uber drivers notified (names, addresses, birth dates, license numbers).
confirmed.status: Confirmed by Uber, Fireworks AI and Notion.

confirmed.summary: Cursor said attackers used an access key stolen from its provider Fireworks AI to copy stored data, then used credentials found in that data to get into other internal systems. On Oct. 29 they used a stolen credential to put malicious copies of a popular extension on Cursor's extension marketplace for about 11 hours.
confirmed.impact: Up to about 5,000 developers may have downloaded the malicious extension, which tried to install hidden SSH backdoors. Cursor says fewer than 0.05% of users had stored coding traces exposed and some customer support data, contact details and archived non-production code were taken.
confirmed.status: Confirmed by Cursor in an incident report (Nov. 14). Exposed credentials rotated and marketplace rebuilt.

confirmed.summary: StubHub International, the non-U.S. ticket resale business run by Ticketbis, told customers it detected unauthorized access to certain systems between late October and early November.
confirmed.impact: Customer names, email addresses, phone numbers and country or region settings may have been exposed. The company says it found no evidence passwords, banking information or payment card details were accessed. It has not said how many customers were affected.
confirmed.status: Confirmed by StubHub International. Investigation ongoing with outside experts.

confirmed.summary: Ethiopian Airlines emailed members of its ShebaMiles frequent-flyer program warning that some customer information may have been exposed in a recent cyberattack it called "of limited scope."
confirmed.impact: The airline says there is currently no evidence financial information was accessed. It has not said when the intrusion happened, what data was involved or how many people are affected.
confirmed.status: Confirmed by Ethiopian Airlines. Investigation ongoing with authorities.

confirmed.summary: Card-skimming code was planted on Fandango's website checkout page and sent payment details typed in by customers to the attackers.
confirmed.impact: Card numbers, CVV codes, expiration dates, billing ZIP codes and email addresses for purchases made October 8-11, 2026. Fandango has not said how many customers were affected.
confirmed.status: Confirmed by Fandango. Notices sent.

confirmed.summary: The networking and security company confirmed hackers accessed company information through a compromised third-party data migration vendor.
