confirmed.impact: Infoblox says there's no indication its products, cloud services or software updates were involved. The Register reports, citing an internal email, that employee personal details (including Social Security numbers and direct-deposit details) and some customers' network configuration backups were taken; Infoblox has not said how many customers are affected.
confirmed.status: Confirmed by Infoblox. Investigation ongoing.

confirmed.summary: Attackers logged into 201 accounts using passwords stolen elsewhere, then exploited a flaw in a scheduling feature to pull customer job details.
confirmed.impact: Up to 366,850 records with customer addresses, phone numbers and request details. No names, emails, passwords or card numbers.
confirmed.status: Confirmed by Meetsmore. Flaw fixed.

confirmed.summary: Unauthorized parties got into a small, isolated part of Swedish beauty retailer Lyko's systems and accessed customer data. Lyko says it stopped the breach within an hour and fixed the security hole.
confirmed.impact: About 60,000 customers across Lyko's markets (36,000 in Sweden): names, addresses and phone numbers. Order information for 95 customers. No ID numbers, payment details or passwords.
confirmed.status: Confirmed by Lyko. Reported to Sweden's privacy regulator (IMY).

confirmed.summary: A systems outage at the Peterborough, N.H. hospital was caused by a cyber incident, hospital leadership said. Network disruptions were first detected on the afternoon of Nov. 8; phones and other systems went down and ambulances were diverted from the ER.
confirmed.impact: Systems disrupted for nearly two weeks; ambulances still diverted. Main campus phones restored, but other systems remain down. Major elective surgeries and outpatient lab and radiology appointments canceled through Nov. 30 (pushed back from Nov. 23). Whether patient or employee data was taken is still under investigation.
confirmed.status: Confirmed by the hospital. On Nov. 20 the CEO said federal authorities were contacted after outside specialists confirmed a cyber incident; no timeline for full restoration. Investigation ongoing.

confirmed.summary: A hacker attack on Kreiskrankenhaus Greiz-Ronneburg in Thuringia caused a system failure noticed on the evening of Nov. 14. The district says the hospital received an extortion message on Nov. 15 and calls the attack an extortion attempt.
confirmed.impact: The emergency room was out of service until the evening of Nov. 16; planned treatments continued. Digital treatment plans were still affected afterward. By Nov. 18 the operating rooms were fully working again, and postponed operations were being made up that week. The hospital has not said whether patient data was affected.
confirmed.status: Attack confirmed by the hospital and the Greiz district. State criminal police and prosecutors are investigating, and police are investigating a suspect. No group has claimed it.

confirmed.summary: Hackers broke into University of Texas at Arlington systems in late October. The school took down MachForms, its online forms portal for event registration, service requests and surveys, and later confirmed that personal information was stolen. The Qilin ransomware gang claimed the attack.
confirmed.impact: Personal information of students and employees stolen; the school has not said what data or how many people. MachForms still offline as of Nov. 13.
confirmed.status: Confirmed by the university. Qilin's claim not confirmed by the school.

confirmed.summary: Charleston County's IT team spotted unusual network activity on Nov. 16 and the county has confirmed data was copied from its systems. The South Carolina Law Enforcement Division (SLED) has deemed the incident criminal and is assisting the investigation.
confirmed.impact: Data removed; the county is still determining whether personal or financial information was involved. Day-to-day operations not affected.
confirmed.status: Confirmed by Charleston County. SLED criminal investigation under way, with state and federal partners.

confirmed.summary: The city shut down its network after discovering a cybersecurity issue; its preliminary assessment points to cybercriminal activity.
confirmed.impact: City Hall and the Assessor's Office remain closed to the public with no reopening date. The main library reopened Nov. 19 on a separate network, but its Wi-Fi, public computers, printing and phones are still down and the Wescott Road branch is closed. The city phone system, in-person card payments, some online portals and mapping services were also disrupted. The city says some city data was affected but most was not accessed.
confirmed.status: Confirmed by the city. Forensic review ongoing with state and federal agencies; the city has not said who was behind it or how its systems were attacked.

confirmed.summary: Hackers pushed fake nuclear and chemical attack warnings to users of Ukraine's air raid alert app. President Zelensky called it a Russian cyberattack.
confirmed.impact: Several fake alerts sent to users' phones before being cleared about an hour later.
confirmed.status: Confirmed by Ukraine's government.

confirmed.summary: Hackers got into the newsroom's website system and newsletter service, posting and emailing fake claims about Zelensky and Putin. The outlet suspects Russia.
confirmed.impact: Four fake emails sent to readers and fake posts on the site (removed). Payment data not at risk.
confirmed.status: Confirmed by The Kyiv Independent.

confirmed.summary: SPH Media, publisher of The Straits Times, found cyberattacks on five of its systems between Nov. 4 and Nov. 8, which it believes were carried out by the same threat actor. It says software bugs and system configuration played a part.
confirmed.impact: About 9% of its database exposed, mostly email addresses plus some names, mailing addresses and phone numbers. No payment card, banking or account access data compromised.
confirmed.status: Confirmed by SPH Media. Reported to Singapore authorities and police.

confirmed.org: Jeonbuk Office of Education school bus system (South Korea)
confirmed.summary: South Korea's Jeonbuk provincial education office said its school bus management system was hacked on the evening of Nov. 15. It learned of the leak after being alerted by the Ministry of Education's cyber safety center, shut the system down and asked police to investigate.
confirmed.impact: Personal data of about 9,900 people leaked, including students' names and addresses, guardians' contact numbers and bus plate numbers. The parent app for live bus tracking and boarding alerts is offline.
confirmed.status: Confirmed by the Jeonbuk Office of Education. Police investigating; victims notified.

confirmed.summary: Ransomware hit an old administrative file server at The Japan Times' group, and data the attacker claimed to have stolen was later posted online.
confirmed.impact: HR and business-partner records from 2001 to August 2022 may be included; reader and payment systems were separate.
confirmed.status: Confirmed by The Japan Times.

confirmed.summary: KARTE, a marketing service run by PLAID that Nikkei uses, was accessed without authorization, and some Nikkei Online Edition user data it handled may have leaked.
confirmed.impact: Email addresses, phone numbers, gender and birth year/month, which Nikkei says had been processed so they can't be restored to their original form. No card data.
confirmed.status: Confirmed by Nikkei.

confirmed.summary: The global market research firm found a breach of one internal information system and filed a complaint with authorities.
confirmed.impact: One internal system. Ipsos says operations weren't affected and the scope is still under investigation.
confirmed.status: Confirmed by Ipsos. Investigation ongoing.

confirmed.summary: Unauthorized access to an outside company that handles SOFT99's online-shop orders and shipping leaked customer order information.
confirmed.impact: About 3,813 people (3,728 orders): names, addresses, phone numbers, emails and order details. No card data. All online shops temporarily closed.
confirmed.status: Confirmed by SOFT99. Police and regulator notified.

confirmed.summary: Kyash says an outsider got into one of its internal web tools for about two and a half hours on Oct. 28 because of an access-control flaw, and may have taken internal documents that included some customer information. It says the Kyash app and card systems were not accessed.
confirmed.impact: Up to 11,996 customers: internal IDs, plus account status and some payment merchant, date and amount details for most of them, and login, top-up or transfer history, device IDs or IP addresses for 310. No names, addresses, phone numbers, emails, card or bank details, or passwords.
confirmed.status: Confirmed by Kyash. Affected customers being emailed.

confirmed.summary: Steinberg, maker of the Cubase music software, says attackers used email and password pairs likely leaked from other, unrelated breaches to break into a limited number of Steinberg accounts (credential stuffing).
confirmed.impact: A limited number of accounts accessed; no count given. Steinberg found no sign account data was changed or software licenses moved or deleted, and accounts with two-factor authentication were not affected. Its own credential database was not compromised.
confirmed.status: Confirmed by Steinberg. Passwords of affected accounts reset; customers being notified.

confirmed.summary: Wieson Technologies says it discovered on Nov. 16 that some of its information system servers had been hit by a cyberattack, and it isolated the affected servers and network equipment.
confirmed.impact: The company says the incident is limited to part of its information systems, core systems and daily operations are running normally, and preliminary checks found no signs of data exfiltration. It is restoring data from backups.
confirmed.status: Confirmed by Wieson Technologies. Investigation into cause and scope ongoing.

confirmed.summary: Botswana's state-owned airline said unauthorized parties got into some of its internal systems in what it described as a suspected ransomware attack.
confirmed.impact: Affected systems hold employee and internal information. The airline says passenger bookings, aircraft systems and flight operations were not affected. It has not said whether data was copied.
confirmed.status: Confirmed by Air Botswana. Investigation ongoing; authorities engaged.

confirmed.summary: The district's superintendent told families the district was hit by a ransomware attack that may have involved a data breach.
confirmed.impact: District laptops and other Windows devices suspended as a precaution; internet, Chromebooks and phones still usable. Whether personal information was accessed is still being determined.
confirmed.status: Confirmed by the district. Investigation ongoing with cybersecurity specialists.

confirmed.org: USEN-ALMEX PreCheck-in (hotel online check-in service, Japan)
confirmed.summary: USEN-ALMEX said attackers hit the system-integration API of PreCheck-in, its online pre-check-in service for hotels, with continuous access starting Nov. 14. It found the unauthorized access on Nov. 15 and shut the service down on Nov. 16. Hotel operators using it, including Solare Hotels and Resorts, are notifying guests.
confirmed.impact: 283 reservations at 26 hotels likely viewed and leaked: names, addresses, phone numbers and email addresses. The company says passport images and credit card data were not included and no secondary damage has been found.
confirmed.status: Confirmed by USEN-ALMEX. Service suspended; investigation ongoing.

confirmed.summary: Hackers replaced the IIHF's homepage with a pro-Russian image and message criticizing Russia's exclusion from international competition. The image was reportedly up for several minutes before the site was taken offline.
confirmed.impact: Website defaced and then kept offline for restoration. No data theft has been reported.
confirmed.status: Confirmed by the IIHF. Investigation ongoing; attackers not identified.

confirmed.summary: Kosé says attackers abused an access-control flaw in the booking system for in-store experiences and lessons at its Maison KOSÉ Ginza and Omotesando shops, sending a rapid stream of requests on Nov. 9 to read members' personal data. On Nov. 19 it disclosed a second leak: customer data it kept in PLAID's KARTE marketing service was taken in the KARTE breach.
confirmed.impact: Booking system: 28,098 customers' names, email addresses, phone numbers, postal codes, addresses, birth dates and gender; no passwords or card data. KARTE: 139,990 ADDICTION brand-site members' names in kana only.
confirmed.status: Confirmed by Kosé. Booking system suspended; reported to police and Japan's privacy regulator.

confirmed.org: PocketChange (currency exchange kiosks and Pokepay, Japan)
confirmed.summary: PocketChange, which runs airport and station kiosks that swap leftover foreign cash for e-money and gift codes, says attackers exploited a vulnerability in a third-party internal business system on Oct. 26, then broke into its operating systems on Nov. 13 and used stolen credentials to reach an old monitoring system of its Pokepay (Enterprise) e-money platform on Nov. 14.
confirmed.impact: Up to 31,462 PocketChange user records (names, phone numbers or emails, member numbers, and passport numbers for up to 24,086), up to 116,361 Pokepay user records (registration details such as phone numbers), 820 merchants' details including bank accounts, codes and PINs for some issued prepaid gift cards, and 58 full card numbers with names from old error logs. The company says no fraudulent transactions have been confirmed.
confirmed.status: Confirmed by PocketChange. Kiosks nationwide suspended since Nov. 17 with no restart date; Pokepay restored Nov. 18; reported to Japan's privacy regulator.

confirmed.org: Yumir Link Cuenote FC (email delivery service, Japan; Peach Aviation, JR Central and others)
confirmed.summary: Tokyo-based Yumir Link found on Oct. 16 that attackers had broken into its Cuenote FC bulk email delivery service. It says they exploited a program vulnerability to steal its support staff's credentials, planted malicious programs on servers to pull data straight from databases, and hijacked logged-in customers' sessions to download address lists through the admin screen. Companies that send mail through Cuenote FC have been announcing leaks since late October.
confirmed.impact: Yumir Link says 47,864,147 delivery-list records (counting overlaps; email addresses, plus names, member IDs and other fields for some) were taken from 49 client systems, and 190 contract-holder records in its Cuenote BASE portal were exposed. Clients reporting leaks include JR Central, JR West and JR Kyushu (about 170,000 Smart EX and Express Reservation members), istyle (@cosme, about 2.8 million customers) and Bandai Namco (346,247 Gundam Base members). On Nov. 20 low-cost airline Peach Aviation said 8,997,106 records of names, birth dates, gender, addresses, phone numbers, email addresses and itineraries leaked; no card or passport data.
confirmed.status: Confirmed by Yumir Link and affected clients. Yumir Link says it was not ransomware and most services are running again; final investigation results pending. Peach reported to Japan's privacy regulator and is notifying customers.

confirmed.org: Japan Digital Agency government file-sharing service (GSS)
confirmed.summary: Japan's Digital Agency says someone other than the intended recipients accessed files on the file-sharing service in its Government Solution Service (GSS), which government agencies use to share large files such as meeting materials with each other and outside parties. It detected the access on Nov. 12, cut the service off from outside networks and stopped it.
confirmed.impact: Access confirmed from July 30 to Nov. 12, 2026. Some uploaded files may have leaked, and the agency says they are expected to include personal information. Number and contents of files not disclosed; no secondary damage confirmed.
confirmed.status: Confirmed by the Digital Agency. Reported to the Personal Information Protection Commission; investigating with police and outside specialists.

confirmed.org: New Zealand Defence Force websites (Force4Families discounts)
confirmed.summary: The New Zealand Defence Force says its website provider notified it on the morning of Friday, Nov. 20 of unauthorized access to its website systems. It took the affected public websites offline and began a forensic investigation.
confirmed.impact: Preliminary findings show a database for the Force4Families Defence Discounts scheme was accessed, containing registered users' names and email addresses. Affected people have been contacted; full extent still being determined.
confirmed.status: Confirmed by NZDF. Privacy Commissioner informed; investigation ongoing.

confirmed.org: Ohio public libraries (Cuyahoga County, Akron-Summit County, Westlake Porter; via vendors)
confirmed.summary: Three Northeast Ohio library systems say attackers got into patron account data through outside vendors that handle customer accounts, checkouts and room reservations. Cuyahoga County Public Library says the incident happened Nov. 15, was discovered the next day and is one of several affecting libraries and vendor systems across the country. The vendors have not been named.
confirmed.impact: Names, home addresses, email addresses, phone numbers, birth dates, usernames and library card numbers (and home branch at two systems). Akron-Summit says, as far as it knows, all its cardholders were affected. The libraries say plain-text passwords and borrowing histories were not accessed. Cuyahoga County and Akron-Summit took their mobile apps offline.
confirmed.status: Confirmed by the libraries. Vendors investigating with outside cybersecurity specialists; patrons urged to reset PINs and passwords.

confirmed.org: AMC Insurance Brokerage claims app AMC air (South Korea)
confirmed.summary: Korean insurance broker AMC (에이엠씨손해보험중개) says outsiders downloaded insurance claim lists and member lists from its AMC air claims app between Nov. 5 and 15. It found the downloads during a security check on Nov. 18, shut the service down the same day and reported it to authorities.
confirmed.impact: Personal data of employees at some client companies: names, employer, full or partial resident registration numbers, relationship to the policyholder and coverage period; for people who filed claims, possibly diagnoses, treatment details and accident descriptions. Number of people and client companies not disclosed.
confirmed.status: Confirmed by AMC in a notice on its website. Claims app suspended; cause and intrusion route under investigation.

confirmed.summary: Tokyo marketing-communications company WOW WORLD says a third party broke into some servers used to run its services and took out part of the client-company data stored on them. It blocked the access and is investigating how the attackers got in.
confirmed.impact: About 49,000 records (counting duplicates), mainly email addresses, belonging to four client companies, which will notify affected people. No card data or My Number IDs confirmed leaked. Services continue.
confirmed.status: Confirmed by WOW WORLD (first report). Reported to authorities; investigation ongoing.

confirmed.summary: On Oct. 11 and 12, attackers took over the remote controls of refrigeration systems at more than 700 retail sites in France, pushing fridges and freezers into abnormal, indefinite defrost cycles and switching off temperature alarms. France has blamed Iran.
confirmed.impact: Hundreds of supermarkets lost perishable stock; the French government says the attacks caused significant material damage, sparked fires and spoiled food worth tens of millions of euros.
confirmed.status: Confirmed by the French government, which on Nov. 9 attributed the attacks to Shahid Kaveh, a cyber unit of Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps, and summoned Iran's ambassador. The Paris prosecutor opened an investigation and requested international arrest warrants for two Shahid Kaveh officials.

confirmed.org: European supermarket refrigeration systems (Delhaize, SuperValu, ICA and others)
confirmed.summary: In the early hours of Nov. 2, a second wave of attacks hit internet-connected refrigeration controls at supermarkets and food businesses in at least 10 European countries, switching fridges and freezers into defrost mode. Around 40 Delhaize stores in Belgium and Luxembourg and 13 SuperValu stores in Ireland were among those hit, and three British meat suppliers were affected through vulnerable Copeland XWEB controllers.
confirmed.impact: Freezer temperatures reportedly rose as high as 50C, forcing retailers to throw away food. In the UK, the affected meat suppliers' units were empty, so no meat was lost. On Nov. 20 it emerged that a UK government and National Cyber Security Centre operation had quietly fixed a separate vulnerability in RDM refrigeration controllers before it could be exploited in UK stores.
confirmed.status: Confirmed as cyberattacks by affected companies, including Sabcobel (which runs Delhaize's systems) and SuperValu owner Musgrave. Belgian federal prosecutors are investigating. No one has claimed responsibility, and authorities have not attributed this wave.

confirmed.summary: The city of Columbia found suspicious activity on its network on Oct. 20 and later confirmed it was a ransomware attack that hit several public-facing services and involved sensitive data on the city's network.
confirmed.impact: MyColaSC, business licensing, planning and development, parks and recreation reservations, GIS and Animal Services went offline; police, fire, 911, Columbia Water and online payments were not affected. All affected applications were restored by Nov. 13. The city has not said what data was accessed or how many people were affected.
confirmed.status: Ransomware attack confirmed by the city. The South Carolina Law Enforcement Division (SLED) is running a criminal investigation.

confirmed.summary: Sunnybrook, a major Toronto hospital, says unauthorized individuals accessed part of its network on Oct. 29 and that data, including some personal health information, was stolen.
confirmed.impact: Number of people and exact data still being determined. The hospital says there is no evidence of widespread access to its electronic medical record or its staff, financial or donor databases. Patient care continued uninterrupted.
confirmed.status: Confirmed by Sunnybrook, which reported it to law enforcement and Ontario's Information and Privacy Commissioner. Affected people will be notified.

confirmed.summary: Bell Financial Group told the Australian stock exchange on Nov. 20 that there had been unauthorized access to a limited number of its IT systems, and that it believes some clients' data was accessed.
confirmed.impact: Some client data likely accessed; the company has not said what data or how many clients. It says client assets are safe and it is operating as usual.
confirmed.status: Confirmed by Bell Financial, which says the incident is contained. The Australian Cyber Security Centre and Australian Federal Police have been notified.

confirmed.summary: Broadcom patched a critical VMware vCenter Server authentication bypass on Nov. 19. Google's Mandiant says a suspected Chinese state-sponsored group it tracks as Armory Castle (formerly UNC5221) had been exploiting it as a zero-day since early September, after first breaking in through BeyondTrust Remote Support appliances.
confirmed.impact: Mandiant observed the attackers creating vCenter administrator accounts, stealing the server's directory database and using tools that can forge authentication tokens to get past multifactor authentication. Number of victims not disclosed.
confirmed.status: Patched by Broadcom (VMSA-2026-0009) as an emergency update. Exploitation documented by Mandiant and Google Threat Intelligence Group; Broadcom has not confirmed exploitation itself.

confirmed.org: Samsung Ads (via advertising data vendor, North America)
confirmed.summary: The n0n ransomware gang dumped 220MB of data it claims belongs to Samsung on its leak site after its deadline ran out. Samsung confirmed a cyber incident at a third-party vendor that supported advertising data processing for its North America Service Business (Samsung Ads), and says the vendor's preliminary investigation indicates some Samsung information may have been affected.
confirmed.impact: Cybernews researchers found about 150,000 Samsung smart TV viewing events from 2024 (timestamps, viewing durations, device details, cities, ZIP codes and TV provider names, but not what individuals watched), about 42,600 political advertising records from September to October 2026, AI ad-model training data and two internal documents. Samsung has not confirmed what data was taken.
confirmed.status: Vendor incident confirmed by Samsung, which is working with the vendor to determine the scope. The vendor has not been named; the gang's claims are unverified.

confirmed.summary: The U.S. Justice Department said Roman Khlynovskiy, 43, a Kazakh national, was extradited from Italy and appeared in federal court in Knoxville, Tennessee, charged over his alleged role in the “8-Digits Team,” a group affiliated with the INC and Lynx ransomware that broke into networks of U.S. schools, hospitals and healthcare providers, stole data and demanded payment not to release it.
confirmed.impact: Victims in at least six states, according to the indictment. Prosecutors say the group boasted of holding more than 50 TB of data with more than 70 million confidential health records, and that its demands totaled more than $500 million.
confirmed.status: Charges announced by the Justice Department; he faces up to 27 years if convicted. An indictment is an allegation and he is presumed innocent. Italian, Ukrainian and Lithuanian authorities assisted.

confirmed.summary: After a researcher published proof-of-concept exploits for more than 30 unpatched flaws in N-able's N-central remote management software, N-able took its hosted N-central environments offline on Nov. 9 and rushed out hotfixes. Attackers then exploited a newer flaw chain, 4EverAble2Shell, to get root access on exposed servers; N-able confirmed it is being used against customers who had not turned off the Legacy API.
confirmed.impact: Security firm Huntback says one attacker installed cryptocurrency mining software on 21 N-central servers, 19 of them already on Hotfix 2, located in the U.S., South Africa, Canada, the U.K., Germany, France and Sweden. N-able said it saw no sign of compromise of its hosted servers. N-central servers manage customers' endpoints, so researchers warn a hit should be treated as a full compromise.
confirmed.status: Attacks confirmed by N-able, which has restricted some features and was rolling out another hotfix (HF3) starting Nov. 16. N-able says this is unrelated to its Mail Assure breach.

confirmed.summary: Hotel and holiday park reservation software provider RMS says it found unauthorized access to a limited part of its environment on Oct. 26. Guests then got WhatsApp, text and email scams quoting their real booking details and asking for card payments.
confirmed.impact: A subset of guest booking information, including guest contact details and reservation details. RMS says credit card and payment details were not involved. Australian accommodation businesses including Kimberley hotels reported guests being targeted.
confirmed.status: Confirmed by RMS. Contained by Nov. 2; as of Nov. 20 RMS is notifying customers whose guest data is confirmed affected. ACSC and the OAIC have been notified.

confirmed.org: Bookeasy (tourism booking platform, Australia; national park bookings)
confirmed.summary: Bookeasy, which runs national park camping and permit bookings for Queensland, Victoria, South Australia and the ACT plus tourism sites like VisitCanberra, detected unauthorized activity on its platform. Park customers then received phishing emails and WhatsApp messages.
confirmed.impact: Customers' names, addresses, email addresses, phone numbers and booking information may have been accessed; Bookeasy says no access to credit card details has been found. The ACT government emailed about 6,000 users. Parks Victoria and the ACT temporarily suspended bookings.
confirmed.status: Confirmed by Bookeasy. On Nov. 20 it said containment is complete and validated by outside experts, the OAIC and ACSC have been notified, and the incident is not connected to the RMS breach.

confirmed.summary: Coles disclosed a cyber security incident in an ASX filing and said it is working with global cyber security experts to contain and secure its IT environment. It has not said what happened.
confirmed.impact: Coles says it has found no evidence that customer, team or supplier data was compromised or removed. Stores and online shopping kept running; some Liquorland click-and-collect issues were being looked into.
confirmed.status: Incident confirmed by Coles, which is working with the Australian Cyber Security Centre. Investigation ongoing.

confirmed.summary: The Oneonta City School District closed schools for two days after a ransomware attack. An email account calling itself Shiba ransomware claimed the attack on Oct. 27 and threatened to publish records of students, parents and staff. In a Nov. 18 message, the superintendent said the forensic investigation is finished and investigators are now reviewing the data.
confirmed.impact: Classes canceled Oct. 23 and Oct. 26. The district has not yet determined whether any personal information was affected; it says it will notify anyone who is.
confirmed.status: Ransomware attack confirmed by the district. Data review ongoing with no timeline; local, state and federal law enforcement investigating.

confirmed.summary: Bell confirmed that what it called an "agentic" threat actor got into some of its systems on Tuesday, Nov. 17, including one used for ordering and supplying telecommunication networks, and stole some enterprise (business) client data. Bell says it quickly contained the attack.
confirmed.impact: Business contact information such as names, corporate email addresses and phone numbers, plus IP addresses. Bell says files and PDFs with more sensitive information were not affected and there was no impact to customer services. Number of affected clients not disclosed.
confirmed.status: Confirmed by Bell, which is contacting affected customers, has shared indicators of compromise with enterprise customers and the Canadian Centre for Cyber Security, and has contacted the RCMP. No one has claimed responsibility.

confirmed.summary: Culture Experience, which runs Japan's TSUTAYA bookstore and media chain business, said it found signs of unauthorized access by a third party to some systems in a data center it uses on Nov. 9 and cut those systems off from the data center. It announced the incident on Nov. 20.
confirmed.impact: Some data in the data center may have leaked; what and how much is still under investigation. The company says the data center does not hold personal information of ordinary TSUTAYA customers. The system shutdown has delayed deliveries to some TSUTAYA stores, and some products are unavailable.
confirmed.status: Confirmed by Culture Experience. Cause and scope under investigation; no date for full recovery.

confirmed.org: Southwire (wire and cable maker, employee health plan)
confirmed.summary: Southwire, the Carrollton, Georgia, maker of electrical wire and cable, is notifying members of its employee health and welfare plan that an unauthorized third party had access to its computer systems between November 2025 and January 2026 and took files. It spotted the suspicious activity on Jan. 29, 2026.
confirmed.impact: Plan members' names, addresses, birth dates, Social Security numbers, medical information and health plan information. Number of people not disclosed.
confirmed.status: Confirmed by Southwire. Letters mailed in November 2026; 24 months of credit monitoring offered. No misuse found.

confirmed.summary: UCHealth, the nonprofit health system based in Aurora, Colorado, said someone got into two employee email accounts in Microsoft's cloud. Suspicious activity was found on July 27, 2026; it announced the breach in November.
confirmed.impact: Names, Social Security numbers, billing information and health information. Total not disclosed; the Texas attorney general was told 873 Texas residents were affected.
confirmed.status: Confirmed by UCHealth, which says the breach was limited to two accounts. Credit monitoring offered.

confirmed.summary: Dexcom, the U.S. maker of continuous glucose monitors, says an unauthorized third party used social engineering to get into certain employee accounts and download files. It determined on Nov. 2 that customers' information may have been involved and began notifying people on Nov. 13.
confirmed.impact: Varies by person: names, addresses, birth dates and health information such as pharmacy, provider, prescription numbers and certain diagnoses, according to the notice filed in California; Washington's attorney general lists Social Security and driver's license numbers among the data for 728 Washington residents. Total number not stated in these filings.
confirmed.status: Confirmed by Dexcom, which revoked the compromised accounts and says it has no sign the information was misused.

confirmed.summary: The University of Copenhagen said hackers exploited a configuration error in a test environment and got into a database of information about the university's users. Staff detected suspicious activity on Oct. 20 and the attack was stopped; the university says the hacker did not reach other systems.
confirmed.impact: About 525,000 current and former students and staff: names, contact details, university usernames and emails, nationality, gender and affiliation, plus encrypted CPR (national ID) numbers that the university says could likely be decrypted because the information needed to do so was also taken. PIN codes for about 20,000 people's ID cards were compromised and reissued. No health or research data believed accessed.
confirmed.status: Confirmed by the university. Reported to police and the Danish Data Protection Agency; affected people notified. Attacker and motive unknown.

confirmed.summary: Leipzig University's IT systems have been largely offline since a cyberattack on Oct. 28. On Nov. 20 the rector said forensic analysis found the attackers had reached 112 virtual servers that departments and institutes rent from the university computing center, for example for research projects.
confirmed.impact: The university says it must assume data on those 112 servers may have been taken and cannot rule out misuse, though it has seen no sign of publication. It says core systems such as AlmaWeb, Moodle, network drives and the mail server were not affected. Around 30,000 students and staff have been hit by the outage of internet services (MDR).
confirmed.status: Confirmed by the university, which is listing potentially affected data on its website. Wi-Fi is due back from Nov. 23, with other services restored in stages.

confirmed.org: Scattered Spider phishing and SIM-swap ring (Tyler Buchanan sentenced)
confirmed.summary: Tyler Buchanan, 24, of Dundee, Scotland, was sentenced on Nov. 17 by a federal judge in Santa Ana, California, to six years in prison. From September 2021 to April 2023 he and co-conspirators sent hundreds of phishing texts to employees of at least a dozen tech, telecom and crypto companies, used stolen logins to get into company systems, and then used SIM swaps to break into individuals' crypto accounts. He is the last of five defendants in the case, which has been linked to the Scattered Spider hacking group.
confirmed.impact: At least $11.6 million in cryptocurrency stolen from victims across the U.S., according to prosecutors; the largest single theft was $1.67 million. Company data taken included confidential work information, account credentials, names, emails and phone numbers (BBC).
confirmed.status: Sentenced after pleading guilty to conspiracy to commit wire fraud and aggravated identity theft; restitution hearing set for Dec. 11. Co-defendants already sentenced.

confirmed.summary: Many USDA applications, including Farm Service Agency loan software, the NRCS ProTracts program that releases farmer payments, and other financial tools for farmers, were knocked offline for about a week. An internal USDA email reported by Nextgov/FCW said its security operations center "uncovered a security incident" that required resetting all database passwords and applications. On Nov. 20, Under Secretary of Agriculture Richard Fordyce told reporters the event was a "cyberthreat," not a "software update."
confirmed.impact: Farmer loans, payments, crop insurance and disaster-relief tools disrupted; staff also had VPN problems. Fordyce said no personally identifiable information was involved and "no data was lost because the systems that protect against cybersecurity threats worked." NBC News, citing sources, reports the agency told employees hackers accessed the system that facilitates payments to farmers. The Dec. 11 ARC/PLC sign-up deadline is not being extended.
confirmed.status: Confirmed as a cyberthreat by a USDA under secretary. Most systems expected back by close of business Nov. 20, with work continuing over the weekend. Attackers not named; USDA's press office has not released a statement.

confirmed.summary: Eskenazi Health, the public hospital division of the Health and Hospital Corporation of Marion County, announced that unauthorized individuals got into the cloud-based work accounts of some employees and accessed patients' electronic health information. Investigators believe the access began June 3; Eskenazi found and cut it off on July 27, Aug. 31 and Sept. 26.
confirmed.impact: Patient information that may have been exposed includes demographic and contact details, health insurance and billing information, medical record numbers, medical and treatment information, sensitive health information and Social Security numbers. Number of affected patients not disclosed. Free credit monitoring offered.
confirmed.status: Confirmed by Eskenazi Health on Nov. 20; notification letters sent to affected patients.

confirmed.summary: Louisiana's largest health provider said an "unauthorized actor" got into two employees' Microsoft accounts between Sept. 18 and Sept. 21 and downloaded files from one of them. Ochsner learned of it on Oct. 1 and hired a forensic firm.
confirmed.impact: Downloaded files may include names, demographic details, Social Security numbers and health information. Ochsner has not said how many people are affected; its data review is ongoing.
confirmed.status: Confirmed by Ochsner on Nov. 19. Letters being mailed; a year of credit monitoring offered where SSNs were involved. Attacker not identified.

confirmed.org: AIRDO (airline, Japan, via email delivery provider)
confirmed.summary: Hokkaido-based airline AIRDO said a third party broke into the outside email delivery system it used, and customers' email addresses leaked through emails sent via that system. It stopped using the system on Oct. 31 and has been switching to a different provider.
confirmed.impact: Up to 673,920 email addresses leaked. AIRDO says no names, addresses, phone numbers, passwords or card data have been found leaked. Booking, flight-status and My AIRDO emails were suspended; some flight-status emails have resumed, and customers are warned about suspicious emails.
confirmed.status: Confirmed by AIRDO (first announced Nov. 4; updated Nov. 20). Email services being restored in stages; investigation with the provider ongoing.

confirmed.summary: Parent company Neighborhood Intelligence said The Container Store restored its website and systems after a cybersecurity incident the previous weekend. Online ordering had been shut down, and stores stayed open using alternative transaction-processing procedures.
confirmed.impact: Online ordering offline and in-store transactions limited for about a week. The company says it does not appear customer financial data was taken. The n0n cybercriminal group had listed the company on its leak site earlier this month (a claim the company did not address). Other Neighborhood Intelligence brands not affected.
confirmed.status: Confirmed by the company; systems restored Nov. 20 with help from outside cybersecurity experts.

confirmed.summary: West Virginia's state legislature is responding to a cybersecurity incident that began Thursday, Nov. 19, took down its website and hit its IT systems. Outside cybersecurity specialists are helping contain and investigate it.
confirmed.impact: Legislature website down; access to some legislative IT systems temporarily disabled. Officials say it appears limited to the Legislature's systems, with no evidence other state agencies are affected. Whether data was taken is not yet known.
confirmed.status: Confirmed by the House of Delegates' Ann Ali. Investigation ongoing; no group has claimed it, and officials did not say whether it was ransomware.

confirmed.summary: Chargemap says an outside party exploited a security flaw in a legacy technical interface on Nov. 8 to extract user account data. It spotted abnormal activity on Nov. 10, fixed the flaw on Nov. 12 and notified France's data protection authority, the CNIL, on Nov. 13.
confirmed.impact: Email addresses, usernames and app language for all affected accounts, plus, where users provided them, names, phone numbers, dates of birth, city and country, profile details and hashed passwords. No bank or payment data, charging history or addresses affected. Affected users were emailed Nov. 18.
confirmed.status: Confirmed by Chargemap; it is filing a complaint and advising users to change passwords.

confirmed.summary: Slovak digital agency ui42 says an attacker used a colleague's compromised login credentials to get into its internal systems, reached sensitive information from some client projects, including former client Dedoles, and then tried to extort the company.
confirmed.impact: Sensitive information from some client projects accessed; ui42 has not said how much or whose. Compromised accounts and keys blocked and client servers checked.
confirmed.status: Confirmed by ui42 on Nov. 20. Reported to law enforcement; ui42 says it will not pay a ransom. Forensic investigation ongoing.

confirmed.org: French precious-metals brokers and crypto tax service (10 charged)
confirmed.summary: Paris prosecutors and France's gendarmerie said ten people were charged on Nov. 19 over the hacking of three precious-metals brokers and a company that helps people declare crypto holdings to tax authorities. Prosecutors say stolen customer data was used for targeted scams: "callers" urged victims to move funds or metals for safekeeping, and others went to victims' homes to collect physical assets.
confirmed.impact: Customer databases stolen from four companies (not named). Prosecutors have not given the number of victims or losses.
confirmed.status: Charged with unauthorized access to data systems, fraud and money laundering as an organized gang, and criminal conspiracy; four held in custody and six under judicial supervision. Suspects are presumed innocent.

confirmed.org: Stolen U.S. government data seller "DP BRUCE" (arrest in Pakistan)
confirmed.summary: Pakistan's National Cyber Crime Investigation Agency said it arrested a suspect in Karachi on Nov. 11 who allegedly used the alias "DP BRUCE" to advertise and sell stolen databases on the LeakBase forum and Telegram, taking payment in cryptocurrency.
confirmed.impact: The agency says the data allegedly included information tied to the FBI, CIA, State Department, Defense Department and various U.S. police departments, plus private businesses. A seized laptop apparently held multiple such databases, according to the agency.
confirmed.status: Arrest announced Nov. 20; case registered under Pakistan's electronic crimes law, including unauthorized access to data. These are allegations; investigation continues.
